### CV-646 — chat.thread_worktree_unbound

Newly authored closed payload contract for `chat.thread_worktree_unbound` 1.0.0: `Plans/dch_event_payloads/chat_thread_worktree_unbound.schema.json#/$defs/project` selects `pm.dch_event.chat_thread_worktree_unbound.project.v1`; `Plans/dch_event_payloads/chat_thread_worktree_unbound.schema.json#/$defs/application` selects `pm.dch_event.chat_thread_worktree_unbound.application.v1`. The root and both payload editions are closed; application and Project are separate schema IDs, never a nullable rewrite of the old swept schema. CV-366/WorkflowScopeV2 scope joins apply: envelope scope_kind equals payload scope.scope_kind; envelope project_id equals scope.project_id, null only for application, with exact Server and storage instance. Freeze actual Computer/thread/root authority from original input, never focus, Settings, HOME or main fallback. EventRecord event_type is `chat.thread_worktree_unbound`, schema/version dispatch selects the exact edition; occurred_at_utc equals ts, actor_ref equals original actor, body transport under SP-337 below, and thread joins the actual original source/committed record. No synthetic run/node/attempt joins. For chat.thread_worktree_unbound, freeze operation_id from the original accepted operation before its effect (fresh entropy for a new operation, retained across retries). The semantic identity tuple is ["chat.thread_worktree_unbound", "1.0.0", storage_instance_id, scope, computer_id, thread_id, operation_id]; use RFC 8785 canonical JSON UTF-8, event_id = "evt_dch_" + SHA-256(tuple). Project idempotency_key = "dch:" + that same hex digest, with CV-365/Storage exact scope_partition = "project~" + unpadded base64url(UTF-8(project_id)); validate encoding and decoded exact Project identity before append or read. Application explicitly adopts CV-366: idempotency_key = "application@1:" + lowercase hex(UTF-8(scope.server_id)) + ":" + lowercase hex(UTF-8(operation_id)). Here owner_operation_id is exactly this family's original operation_id, frozen with the accepted source before any effect; no retry, timestamp, focus or result component is added. No additional optional effect component is defined for this family; distinct event types retain separate Storage lifetime tuples (scope_partition,event_type,idempotency_key). Exact original Server/Computer/thread/source joins remain mandatory, including on same-key retries. Same operation and semantic digest returns the original result and first receipt without a new effect; a different digest conflicts; missing authoritative dedupe yields dedupe_unavailable with zero new effect. Application must never use the Project dch: recipe. Capture original payload and EventRecord semantic digest; same identity with changed semantics is a conflict, never an overwrite. Unknown version or scope is quarantined/unavailable. Earlier shape-only schemas remain unadopted. A payload change requires a new version/edition and governed migration; readers never rewrite original identities or payload bytes.

Adopt SP-337 for this exact event body. The logical body remains the selected closed Project/application payload edition, with its existing string and array bounds unchanged and the integer domain specified below. Encode that complete body as SP-236 canonical MessagePack (recursive exact UTF-8 map-key order and shortest encodings); measure encoded bytes, not JSON characters or the envelope. At most 16384 bytes may be inline with payload_ref=null. An oversized inline body is refused before append. Larger or separately governed bodies use payload={} and the newly authored string binding `payload:v1:{lowercase_blake3_64}:{decimal_byte_size}:application/msgpack` in EventRecord.payload_ref, with canonical unsigned decimal size, selecting the existing payload-pack index key `payload:v1:{lowercase_blake3_64}`. The reference commits to the BLAKE3 of the exact complete encoded body, exact byte size and media type application/msgpack. Resolve and decode that original body, validate its exact schema/edition and every scope/identity/actor/time join as for inline bodies; a reference is never an empty semantic body. Require actual original Storage instance, Server/scope/Computer/thread custody, current authorization/deletion/hold access checks, durable exact pack bytes and index entry and verified readback before the referencing append can be acknowledged or its first receipt/result published. Missing, changed, unauthorized, deleted, wrong-store or unreadable body/index evidence refuses publication; no base64 body, truncated body, alternate-source reconstruction or rerun is allowed. Pack durability, reference counts, holds, backups and deletion deadlines remain SP-337; this binding grants no new retention exemption.

This family selects current replay_policy=dedupe_by_idempotency_key for ordinary writes and retries. Reject projector_replay_only as replay_only_not_appendable before dedupe, even if both retry records use it; its separate compatibility-reader behavior remains the EventRecord owner rule and never authorizes a current append. Compute producer_semantic_digest using only the exact caller-supplied EventRecord semantic field list in the EventRecord owner clause, with its RFC 8785/SHA-256 recipe, including payload and payload_ref in their original transport form. Exclude only the Storage-assigned sequence_id, observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc from this comparison; metadata-only variation returns the original result/first receipt. Global event_id integrity is a separate mandatory check: same scoped key with a changed event_id, or same event_id with another lifetime identity or semantic body, conflicts. Every included semantic field is independently mutation-tested; no whole-record equality substitutes for the owner commitment.

For new writes and current identity/idempotency inputs, this family selects strict-v4 exact integer types with the owner-declared domain of each field. Storage sequence_id and its last_sequence_id copies, frontier_revision, selected_segment_generation, manifest_generation, recovery_epoch and pack byte_size retain exact uint64 values 0 through 18446744073709551615; no 2^53 ceiling applies to Storage metadata. Publication revision and logical payload integers retain their existing owner minima and maxima, with no invented DCH safe-integer cap. Declared integer slots reject runtime float/string/bool/null/array/object substitutes except explicitly nullable slots. Storage metadata is excluded from the producer-semantic projection as already specified. The producer route is the CV-1100 qualified RFC 8785 encoding of the unchanged CV-317 producer projection (shared producer_semantic_bytes/producer_semantic_digest); an unsupported exact producer input is a structured route refusal, without narrowing its logical owner domain, rounding or stringification. Physical bytes follow SP-236 through the shared SP-1100 codec (storage_value_bytes, EVENT_VALUE profile): float type, minimal exact float width and signed zero are preserved, so a lexical alias never shares an integer's bytes, and the exact integer slots refuse every alias; invalid JSON 01 refuses under the CV-1100 current parser. Retained-recipe dispatch composes the shared SP-1101 RetainedDispatcher and timestamps use the shared CV-1101 check, as the retained-original and format paragraphs state. Test Storage write/retry inputs at 2^53, 2^60 and uint64 maximum, and refuse overflow, negative and wrong-type metadata independently.

Retained and compatibility originals use the schema, numeric domain, runtime type policy, format validator and physical encoder in force when written. The single selector record_number_rule() owns this dispatch on passive history, SP-337 materialization/reference verification, full-index source/checkpoint validation, checkpoint physical storage, saved-original retry comparison and terminal retained-start lookup. New/current inputs select strict-v4. For retained sources, independently read protected Storage write-receipt provenance binds actual storage_instance_id, exact original source-value SHA-256 and recipe_id; it is committed with the original write and survives restore with that source. Candidate fields, caller version/recipe flags, mutable live state and payload content cannot select or enroll an earlier recipe. Verify any claim against that independently authenticated provenance, then verify the exact original bytes with the selected recipe. Missing earlier provenance is unavailable under that earlier recipe, never a guessed downgrade: an original of a Store outside the sealed write custody refuses as unavailable and a receipt naming a recipe with no installed frozen verifier refuses as unsupported, with no fallback to another recipe; within a custody Store an original without a legacy receipt was written by the current strict-v4 writer. Each retained read composes the shared SP-1101 RetainedDispatcher once: one owner selection, no caller override and no current-then-legacy probing, and the installed frozen verifier of that exact recipe tuple (pinned to the recipe's recorded original schema hashes) checks the original. Preserve raw-v1 (d36809af original MessagePack numeric types), normalized-v2 (a785466d normalized integral floats with the original uncapped integer domain), and strict-v3 (c21fa62e safe integers; its original checker skipped date-time and URI formats); Plans/dch_retained_recipes.json pins their exact original schemas and source revisions. A skipped format check never authenticates invalid history (CV-1101, SP-1101): frozen validators apply the shared date-time predicate and CV-253 to the recipe's pinned original resources, so a retained timestamp CV-1101 refuses is owner-invalid and refuses, while owner-valid lowercase, leap-second and long-fraction history stays readable with its exact spelling; the skipped URI check is preserved. Never re-encode raw-v1 bytes under a later normalization to verify their commitment. Plans/dch_write_recipe_receipts.json is an independent synthetic Storage receipt adapter, not native authentication evidence. Every earlier-valid retained numeric or format record stays readable with current authorization, deletion/hold access, withdrawal and actual-source identity checks. A forged source or recipe selection still refuses. Current derived checkpoints may copy an old event sequence into their exact new integer representation; the original retained event/index sequence and commitment remain unchanged. A retry verifies its saved original through the same historical schema/byte/custody reader before comparison; its incoming input stays strict-v4, and a replay-only compatibility original still cannot authorize a current append or retry. Different earlier semantic values conflict without sending an out-of-current-domain original through the current RFC 8785 encoder. A retained checkpoint, including its history and physical payload pack, uses its own original write provenance separately from its referenced event.

The strict-v4 format validators are mandatory and installed explicitly, never through optional jsonschema plugins. Timestamps adopt the shared CV-1101 check: every current and frozen DCH validator is pm_event_datetime.datetime_validator over the complete outer schema, so the registered RFC 3339 predicate runs through the validator. occurred_at_utc keeps the EventRecord profile (T or t, Z/z or a signed offset, any fraction length, year 0000 and legitimate offset-adjusted leap seconds); observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc keep CV-253's storage_utc_z profile through the inventory-classified envelope; the family ts and populated checkpoint retired_at_utc take the same predicate with their unchanged owner-schema terminal uppercase-Z pattern. A missing zone, space or wrong separator, invalid calendar field, hour 24, minute 60, false leap second, empty fraction and trailing LF refuse. Timestamp strings are never rewritten and are compared only as exact strings; no DCH-local timestamp grammar remains. PR URLs where declared fully match RFC 3986 HTTPS syntax, including valid percent escapes, reg-name or bracketed IPv6/IPvFuture host, numeric port and path/query/fragment grammar. Malformed brackets/hosts/escapes and whitespace refuse. No PR-host allowlist or new provider behavior is introduced. UUID contexts keep Storage's enforced descriptor. Both payload editions, all three EventRecord timestamps and populated checkpoint retirement times have isolated format negatives; applicable PR payloads cover every malformed URL form.

Retained and compatibility originals use the schema, numeric domain, runtime type policy, format validator and physical encoder in force when written. The single selector record_number_rule() owns this dispatch on passive history, SP-337 materialization/reference verification, full-index source/checkpoint validation, checkpoint physical storage, saved-original retry comparison and terminal retained-start lookup. New/current inputs select strict-v4. For retained sources, independently read protected Storage write-receipt provenance binds actual storage_instance_id, exact original source-value SHA-256 and recipe_id; it is committed with the original write and survives restore with that source. Candidate fields, caller version/recipe flags, mutable live state and payload content cannot select or enroll an earlier recipe. Verify any claim against that independently authenticated provenance, then verify the exact original bytes with the selected recipe. Missing earlier provenance is unavailable under that earlier recipe, never a guessed downgrade: an original of a Store outside the sealed write custody refuses as unavailable and a receipt naming a recipe with no installed frozen verifier refuses as unsupported, with no fallback to another recipe; within a custody Store an original without a legacy receipt was written by the current strict-v4 writer. Each retained read composes the shared SP-1101 RetainedDispatcher once: one owner selection, no caller override and no current-then-legacy probing, and the installed frozen verifier of that exact recipe tuple (pinned to the recipe's recorded original schema hashes) checks the original. Preserve raw-v1 (d36809af original MessagePack numeric types), normalized-v2 (a785466d normalized integral floats with the original uncapped integer domain), and strict-v3 (c21fa62e safe integers; its original checker skipped date-time and URI formats); Plans/dch_retained_recipes.json pins their exact original schemas and source revisions. A skipped format check never authenticates invalid history (CV-1101, SP-1101): frozen validators apply the shared date-time predicate and CV-253 to the recipe's pinned original resources, so a retained timestamp CV-1101 refuses is owner-invalid and refuses, while owner-valid lowercase, leap-second and long-fraction history stays readable with its exact spelling; the skipped URI check is preserved. Never re-encode raw-v1 bytes under a later normalization to verify their commitment. Plans/dch_write_recipe_receipts.json is an independent synthetic Storage receipt adapter, not native authentication evidence. Every earlier-valid retained numeric or format record stays readable with current authorization, deletion/hold access, withdrawal and actual-source identity checks. A forged source or recipe selection still refuses. Current derived checkpoints may copy an old event sequence into their exact new integer representation; the original retained event/index sequence and commitment remain unchanged. A retry verifies its saved original through the same historical schema/byte/custody reader before comparison; its incoming input stays strict-v4, and a replay-only compatibility original still cannot authorize a current append or retry. Different earlier semantic values conflict without sending an out-of-current-domain original through the current RFC 8785 encoder. A retained checkpoint, including its history and physical payload pack, uses its own original write provenance separately from its referenced event.

The strict-v4 format validators are mandatory and installed explicitly, never through optional jsonschema plugins. Timestamps adopt the shared CV-1101 check: every current and frozen DCH validator is pm_event_datetime.datetime_validator over the complete outer schema, so the registered RFC 3339 predicate runs through the validator. occurred_at_utc keeps the EventRecord profile (T or t, Z/z or a signed offset, any fraction length, year 0000 and legitimate offset-adjusted leap seconds); observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc keep CV-253's storage_utc_z profile through the inventory-classified envelope; the family ts and populated checkpoint retired_at_utc take the same predicate with their unchanged owner-schema terminal uppercase-Z pattern. A missing zone, space or wrong separator, invalid calendar field, hour 24, minute 60, false leap second, empty fraction and trailing LF refuse. Timestamp strings are never rewritten and are compared only as exact strings; no DCH-local timestamp grammar remains. PR URLs where declared fully match RFC 3986 HTTPS syntax, including valid percent escapes, reg-name or bracketed IPv6/IPvFuture host, numeric port and path/query/fragment grammar. Malformed brackets/hosts/escapes and whitespace refuse. No PR-host allowlist or new provider behavior is introduced. UUID contexts keep Storage's enforced descriptor. Both payload editions, all three EventRecord timestamps and populated checkpoint retirement times have isolated format negatives; applicable PR payloads cover every malformed URL form.

### CV-647 — chat.response_stop_requested — closed payload and replay

Newly authored payload contract for chat.response_stop_requested 1.0.0 under DL-045/DL-406/DL-427. Plans/dch_stop_request.schema.json selects closed Project pm.dch_stop.request.project.v1 and application pm.dch_stop.request.application.v1 editions, version 1.0.0. Required fields are exactly schema_id, schema_version, thread_id, operation_id, actor_ref, ts, computer_id, scope, assistant_turn_id, stop_reason_code and target_work. WorkflowScopeV2 and existing Chat thread/non-secret-reference and Storage-instance descriptors are reused; target_work item fields are exactly kind, work_ref and lease_ref. The original accepted cmd.chat.stop source fixes the actual reply and complete target list. References contain no credentials, instructions, transcript bodies, raw output or newly copied evidence. The Stop reason is a code, never arbitrary diagnostic text. Unknown fields/editions, forged targets and cross-scope sources refuse. run_id, node_id and attempt_id in this request's EventRecord are null: an optional command run selector resolves to the actual assistant turn and does not invent a Goal join. EventRecord event_type equals this exact family, payload_schema_id selects the exact edition, scope_kind/project_id/thread_id/actor_ref/occurred_at_utc join the original body (ts is request occurrence time), and global event_id and scoped key recompute by ACD-627 against the independently read actual Storage instance.

Current writes and incoming retries select dedupe_by_idempotency_key; projector_replay_only refuses as replay_only_not_appendable before dedupe, including when both retry inputs claim it. Retained compatibility-reader records may use that historical policy and never authorize current append. The producer-semantic commitment adopts the EventRecord owner's exact 21 caller-supplied fields and RFC 8785/SHA-256 recipe, excluding only Storage-assigned sequence_id, observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc; those are verified from independently read original Storage bytes on reads, never trusted from payload. Metadata-only incoming retry variation returns original evidence; every included semantic field and independent global-ID check remains mandatory. No serializer, number cap or timestamp grammar is added here. Adopt SP-236's owner domains and physical recipe; unsupported producer RFC 8785 inputs are unavailable without rounding, retyping or narrowing Storage uint64. Mandatory format validation uses pm_dch_formats.validator: the shared CV-1101 datetime_validator for the declared date-time descriptors (EventRecord and CV-253 profiles; the Stop ts and outcome_at_utc keep their terminal-Z owner pattern) and Storage's enforced UUID descriptor; malformed and trailing-LF inputs refuse. The Stop contract has one current edition, so SP-1101 retained dispatch selects no earlier recipe for it.

Adopt SP-337 explicitly for this exact body: at most 16384 encoded SP-236 bytes inline with payload_ref null; above that, or separately governed content, payload is {} and payload_ref is payload:v1:{lowercase_blake3_64}:{canonical_unsigned_decimal_byte_size}:application/msgpack. Resolve the existing payload:v1:{lowercase_blake3_64} index in the actual same Storage instance. Recompute BLAKE3, exact byte count and media type from complete original bytes, verify scope/Computer/thread and current authorization/deletion/hold access, durable pack/index and exact readback before acknowledgement or publication. Measure every stored part including the pointer; no truncation, base64 substitute or unverified inline exception. Logical target-work counts remain those of the actual reply, with no new lane cap. Replay reads original evidence only, never resends cancellation or reruns work. Original versions remain byte-exact; a later schema/physical recipe is separately versioned and authenticated by original write provenance, never selected by a caller's downgrade flag. Unsupported or missing original provenance is unavailable. Writer withdrawal cuts this exact family off before new operations, fences its readers/affected index publication, keeps supported historical lookup under current custody, and requires a separately versioned fresh SP-278 rebuild before successor publication; no reminting, in-place rewriting or source-log deletion.

## CV-500 — attempt.completed prepared Event Authority contract

Newly authored owner contract: `attempt.completed@1.0.0` uses the independently closed schema `Plans/event_payload_attempt_completed.schema.json` (schema id `https://puppetmaster.local/schemas/event_payloads/attempt_completed/1.0.0`). It is a proposed payload version only, and grants no current write permission. Required, optional and closed enum fields in that schema reconcile this family's existing minima; additional fields and wrong versions reject. Shape descriptors are redacted structural labels, opaque refs are not retrieval authority, and freeform reason/outcome codes must resolve their actual owner domain; no secrets, source bodies, local absolute paths or capability content may be embedded.

For `attempt.completed` independently, every timestamp (including nested score observations) must consume its entire RFC3339 UTC string through the final Z, without stripping, normalization or ignored trailing LF/CR/whitespace. Date/time validity remains mandatory. The exact-end schema guard and full-string format checker both apply; source-consistent trailing-LF negatives and isolated schema-field negatives run through the full semantic checker.


`project_id` equals EventRecord.project_id and scope_partition is the Storage project partition for that exact Project. Every payload run_id/thread_id/attempt_id equals the corresponding envelope value when present; no fabricated node/attempt for pre-attempt work. Existing runtime snapshot refs resolve immutable pm.requested_effective_runtime with its package/seam/lane/worktree/account joins; execution_unit_context_ref resolves the versioned Executor schema. All present refs must resolve under source permission/deletion checks. Conditional minima in EP-210 remain normative beyond schema shape checks.

Exact legacy alias for this family: `none`. Import normalization uses Case L-5's existing legacy identity recipe, preserves original bytes/IDs and records source provenance; current writers reject aliases and unsupported revisions. Current writes use the schema above only after separate family admission; no upgrading old payloads on read or silent enum/string substitution.

Pass-two source contract for `attempt.completed`: EP-210 and `executor.attempt_completed.source_adapter.v1@1.0.0` bind every source join and conditional presence; the exact companion row supplies the lifecycle table and source roles. Static normalized read captures in `Plans/executor_event_semantic_fixtures.json` are not runtime packets or persisted schema substitutes. Existing payload version/schema, closed enum domains, whole runtime/execution schemas and historical import provenance remain authoritative. No silent alias, discarded original discriminator or missing join may enter a current writer. Run `python3 scripts/pm_executor_event_semantics.py` for this family's own source/transition and receipt/replay/withdrawal oracles.

For `attempt.completed` independently, current timestamps use the complete UTC grammar `[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}[Tt][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(?:\.[0-9]+)?Z`, with Gregorian calendar validity, hours 00..23, minutes/seconds 00..59, and one or more fractional digits when the dot is present. Leap seconds, missing zones, alternate separators/basic dates, out-of-range dates/times and trailing bytes reject. The standalone schema boundary enforces calendar validity without an optional format plugin. ```yaml
plan_unit_id: CV-650

  DL-045, searched independently in reports/event-authority-20261104/DMEM-search.json. Payload schema Plans/memory_maintenance_event_payloads.schema.json#/$defs/memory_dedup_sweep_completed
  is a distinct closed definition; schema_version and event_type are exact constants. All listed properties are
  required and unknown properties fail. Project id must equal the project_only EventRecord envelope, operation_id
  must equal its correlation_id, causation_event_id is the same-operation started_event_id. Source revision is the
  hash of the frozen canonical corpus revision selected at acceptance; a current snapshot substituted on retry fails.
  occurred_at_utc is strict UTC and is frozen at first logical publication, not retry time. Inline payload only;
  payload_ref=null. The producer validates root, dates, permission, joins and no-secret metadata before append.
  Completed result_ref/hash use this family's SP-bound memresult_ identity and immutable operation outcome;
  status/ref/hash and frozen time must exactly equal the operation and retained original full value. The ref never grants body access. Reject terminal-before-start, mismatched Project/operation/source revision, missing receipt, changed request
  bytes or unsupported version. Event identity and ordered recovery are defined for this family by SP-630, not borrowed
  from another event.

  DL-444 and DL-445 apply E-CARDS-2 Card 6.a and 6.b option A. Among owner-eligible identical embed_text_hash memories, keep the oldest by original created_at, breaking a tie by the unchanging note ID (lexical id order). Preserve every original EvidenceRef and the merge record identifying every original and the survivor; the survivor retains the union of evidence references. Archive the other eligible originals with their original identities, evidence references, versions and links to the survivor intact. They remain available in history and are never automatically deleted. Only the user deletes memories. Pinned memories stay excluded; skip any merge that pin protection forbids. These decisions do not broaden existing eligibility or scope, admit a writer, settle operation retention or bypass start custody. Scores for separate archive jobs do not select a duplicate survivor. ```yaml
plan_unit_id: CV-675

  dev_session_record.v1 versioned aggregate value binding (newly authored technical closure, DL-045). Section15 owns the developer workflow (209,244-247,9433); Shared Runtime 10.1 owns subordinate DebugSessionBroker mechanics. The physical key remains dev_session_record.v1:{project_id}:{dev_session_id}, value version 2.0.0, schema pm.storage_value.dev_session_record.v2 at Plans/ds15_dev_session_record_v2.schema.json#/$defs/dev_session_record. No parallel root identity or fabricated DAP id. workflow carries its state/revision/operation/outcome and actual optional run/thread/workspace/terminal links; dap is null for non-debug work, else the unchanged complete DAP v1 value with its independent generation/state/waiter evidence. Outer and nested project_id/dev_session_id and DAP topology.project_id must agree. Workflow state is never used as DAP state or PTY liveness. A DAP state change needs its own verified DebugSessionBroker outcome and existing waiter/trigger checks; workflow stop alone authorizes none.

After restart verify runtime owners before any mutation. Writer/reader withdrawal follows each event contract. SP-339/SP-340 existing canonical projects_and_sources profile and 16384-byte encoded ceiling remain. Retention for the expanded v2 workflow/DAP combination is PENDING_RETENTION_DECISION for RT; existing DAP-only v1 remains RP-DEBUG-30D under its unchanged scope, never extended to workflow by inference. Runtime state created/loading/ready/stale/degraded/error/closed belongs to the actual live PreviewSession, not this UI cache. Opening/revealing preserves runtime identity when the existing subject/source_revision/surface-kind/transport tuple is unchanged; source changes use owner-resolved identity, never a guessed old live session.   negative-zero tokens and leading zeros before schema/semantic use, identity hashing or retry comparison; never coerce
  retained originals, whose write-time recipe SP-1101 selects. Storage-assigned sequence/frontier fields retain their u64
  physical domain (SP-1100), with the same exact integer representation. Timestamps follow CV-1101 through the shared date_time predicate with the owner profile of each field. Payload,
  state and record date-time fields, EventRecord occurred_at_utc and the first-receipt acknowledged_at_utc take the

  trailing LF or illegitimate second 60 refuses), and the two Storage-assigned EventRecord instants that CV-253
  binds take its storage_utc_z profile. Strings are never rewritten; instants compare exactly with offsets applied, every
  fractional digit kept and a leap second ordered within its minute. Enforce date-time and UUID formats without

### CV-780 - browser.session.created identity replay and withdrawal

```yaml
plan_unit_id: CV-780
unit_type: interface_contract
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Contracts_V0.md
canonical_text: 'Newly authored owner contract, exactly browser.session.created@1.0.0. Adopt Contracts_V0#EventRecord
  2.0.0 and its complete producer_semantic_digest recipe unchanged, plus SP-026/SP-236 SeglogFrameV2 and SP-286/CV-339
  strict full-value v2 first-AppendReceipt custody. No local envelope or digest is created. Exact family payload/schema
  routing is Plans/card2_event_payloads.schema.json#/$defs/browser_session_created; Project pm.browser.session.created.payload.v1
  and application pm.browser.session.created.payload.application.v1, version 1.0.0, must match actual scope. Envelope
  Project/thread/Run/Attempt joins match the genuine source; non-execution manual operations have Run/Attempt null
  together and no invented node. The existing owner first reserves one original operation ID with its immutable
  source and event obligation; that ID is unique for the lifetime of its actual Home Server and survives restart/recovery/backup.
  Its per-effect component is exact UTF-8 event_type + '':'' + original operation ID. Application idempotency is
  exactly application@1:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(component)} under CV-366; Project uses card2@1:{hex(server_id)}:{hex(component)}
  within the unchanged (scope_partition,event_type,idempotency_key) lifetime. Project partition is project~ plus
  unpadded base64url of exact UTF-8 project_id; application is app. Global event_id is ''card2:'' followed by colon-separated
  lowercase UTF-8 hex of storage_instance_id, server_id, original operation ID and exact event_type. It is reserved
  once, never regenerated from observation/retry time, and cannot be reused for another semantic event. Lost original
  identity never authorizes a new one.

  The producer-owned semantic comparison is precisely the central EventRecord recipe: caller-supplied semantics
  only; exclude Storage-assigned sequence_id, observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc. Same identity/same semantic
  digest returns the original event/result with zero new effects; a different semantic digest is idempotency_conflict;
  authoritative dedupe unavailable is dedupe_unavailable with zero append/effects. Never select or accept projector_replay_only
  on current append or retry: reject replay_only_not_appendable. Compatibility reading it grants no write/effect
  permission. No-op, failed, refused or unknown owner outcome cannot claim a successful event. After actual family
  admission, order is authenticated owner acceptance/reservation, canonical owner body commit and durable event
  obligation, ordinary Storage append/commit-frame issuance under SP-286, exact first receipt custody, then dependent
  terminal result publication. Pending event obligations retain their original source and retry only append resolution;
  no crash reruns a browser effect or memory edit. An unavailable family refuses execution before a history-dependent
  change; these drafts grant no native writer.

  Compatibility dispatch is exact family/version/schema ID; unrecognized successors quarantine instead of guessing
  or translating a retired spelling. Preserve retained original records and their original source custody; migration
  is forward-only with a separately governed successor. Withdrawal sets an explicit writer admission cutoff before
  stopping the old producer, drains or fences original pending obligations through SP-286, removes that version
  from live acceptance and reader publication, invalidates reader caches, and rebuilds only generic derived metadata
  from still-admitted genuine sources. A removed reader is fenced even for historical events; an authorized retained
  historical reader does not compare the old transition to today''s subject state. Restore preserves cutoff/withdrawal
  and original results; missing source, ambiguous version, incoherent backup, forged receipt or withdrawn source
  refuses. This unit grants no registration and no native proof.

  Before retry returns or recovers an original, authenticate its exact EventRecord from Storage and validate
  its envelope, family/version/payload schema, recomputed event/idempotency identity, original immutable owner
  records and original transition. Verify the original observation byte-for-value against that record; verify
  sequence_id, observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc independently against the Storage-issued first receipt,
  including integer bounds and real timestamp syntax/calendar validity. These assigned fields remain excluded
  from caller-semantic equality. A changed candidate observation time or sequence does not create a conflict;
  a forged original or receipt never becomes the original result. Historical original validation uses its original
  accepted schema/policy, including genuine compatibility replay-only history, without current live-state or
  current-writer policy guards. Current candidate append/retry still refuses replay_only_not_appendable, and
  withdrawn, forged, foreign or unavailable custody refuses on every path.

  Numbers, sweep 2026-11-10 (CV-1100 beside the unchanged CV-317 and CV-366 recipes): browser.session.created
  current inputs enter only as exact integer tokens (a -0 token is refused at parsing), and every EventRecord and
  payload integer slot admits only an exact current integer, so an integral float such as 1.0, 1e0 or -0.0 is
  refused at the slot. The retry comparison is the shared qualified producer projection (producer_semantic_bytes /
  producer_semantic_digest); a projection that RFC 8785 cannot carry exactly, for example producer_sequence_id
  2^53+1, 2^60 or 2^64-1, is refused before any append or owner effect, while 2^53 encodes exactly. Storage-
  assigned sequence_id follows SP-1100 and stays outside producer semantics. The idempotency, event_id and CV-366
  key recipes are unchanged. Timestamps and retained originals, sweep 2026-11-11 (CV-1101 beside CV-253 and CV-317;
  SP-1101): every timestamp field uses the shared CV-1101 date_time predicate with its owner''s profile, never a
  lane grammar. occurred_at_utc and payload ts take the broad event_record profile (T or t, Z, z or an hh:mm
  offset, legitimate leap seconds, any fraction length); Storage-assigned observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc also
  take CV-253''s storage_utc_z profile (terminal uppercase Z only), on the current record, the retry original and
  retained history alike. A retry original and a retained history read are first resolved once through the shared
  SP-1101 RetainedDispatcher from Storage''s sealed write custody (static stand-in
  Plans/card2_original_custody.json, never a request field): a Store outside that custody refuses as
  original_unavailable and a sealed recipe without an installed frozen verifier as recipe_unknown, with no
  fallback, current-then-legacy probing or caller override. The only write-time recipe is card2@1, whose tuple pins
  the EventRecord and family payload schema bytes and these field profiles. Owner-valid lowercase, offset,
  leap-second and long-fraction history stays readable with its exact spelling; an offset or lowercase-z Storage
  timestamp never becomes valid history.
'
gui_related: false
gui_classification_reason: Defines event semantics, metadata and custody for existing behavior; no visual presentation.
depends_on:
- CV-317
- CV-339
- CV-366
unblocks: []
acceptance_criteria:
- owner_change_id is the authenticated canonical change identity shared across overlapping owner routes, never an after-record reference. Same operation and owner_change_id cannot record the same fact in both vocabularies; distinct real changes retain distinct identities.
- Canonical semantic digest and CV-366 app key remain exact.
- Current append and retry reject projector_replay_only; all family identity/receipt/withdrawal negatives reject.
validation_surfaces:

negative_constraints:

  Its per-effect component is exact UTF-8 event_type + '':'' + original operation ID. Application idempotency is

  within the unchanged (scope_partition,event_type,idempotency_key) lifetime. Project partition is project~ plus
  unpadded base64url of exact UTF-8 project_id; application is app. Global event_id is ''card2:'' followed by colon-separated
  lowercase UTF-8 hex of storage_instance_id, server_id, original operation ID and exact event_type. It is reserved
  once, never regenerated from observation/retry time, and cannot be reused for another semantic event. Lost original
  identity never authorizes a new one.

  The producer-owned semantic comparison is precisely the central EventRecord recipe: caller-supplied semantics
  only; exclude Storage-assigned sequence_id, observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc. Same identity/same semantic
  digest returns the original event/result with zero new effects; a different semantic digest is idempotency_conflict;
  authoritative dedupe unavailable is dedupe_unavailable with zero append/effects. Never select or accept projector_replay_only
  on current append or retry: reject replay_only_not_appendable. Compatibility reading it grants no write/effect
  permission. No-op, failed, refused or unknown owner outcome cannot claim a successful event. After actual family
  admission, order is authenticated owner acceptance/reservation, canonical owner body commit and durable event
  obligation, ordinary Storage append/commit-frame issuance under SP-286, exact first receipt custody, then dependent
  terminal result publication. Pending event obligations retain their original source and retry only append resolution;
  no crash reruns a browser effect or memory edit. An unavailable family refuses execution before a history-dependent
  change; these drafts grant no native writer.

  Compatibility dispatch is exact family/version/schema ID; unrecognized successors quarantine instead of guessing
  or translating a retired spelling. Preserve retained original records and their original source custody; migration
  is forward-only with a separately governed successor. Withdrawal sets an explicit writer admission cutoff before
  stopping the old producer, drains or fences original pending obligations through SP-286, removes that version
  from live acceptance and reader publication, invalidates reader caches, and rebuilds only generic derived metadata
  from still-admitted genuine sources. A removed reader is fenced even for historical events; an authorized retained
  historical reader does not compare the old transition to today''s subject state. Restore preserves cutoff/withdrawal
  and original results; missing source, ambiguous version, incoherent backup, forged receipt or withdrawn source
  refuses. This unit grants no registration and no native proof.

  Before retry returns or recovers an original, authenticate its exact EventRecord from Storage and validate
  its envelope, family/version/payload schema, recomputed event/idempotency identity, original immutable owner
  records and original transition. Verify the original observation byte-for-value against that record; verify
  sequence_id, observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc independently against the Storage-issued first receipt,
  including integer bounds and real timestamp syntax/calendar validity. These assigned fields remain excluded
  from caller-semantic equality. A changed candidate observation time or sequence does not create a conflict;
  a forged original or receipt never becomes the original result. Historical original validation uses its original
  accepted schema/policy, including genuine compatibility replay-only history, without current live-state or
  current-writer policy guards. Current candidate append/retry still refuses replay_only_not_appendable, and
  withdrawn, forged, foreign or unavailable custody refuses on every path.

  current inputs enter only as exact integer tokens (a -0 token is refused at parsing), and every EventRecord and
  payload integer slot admits only an exact current integer, so an integral float such as 1.0, 1e0 or -0.0 is
  refused at the slot. The retry comparison is the shared qualified producer projection (producer_semantic_bytes /
  producer_semantic_digest); a projection that RFC 8785 cannot carry exactly, for example producer_sequence_id
  2^53+1, 2^60 or 2^64-1, is refused before any append or owner effect, while 2^53 encodes exactly. Storage-
  assigned sequence_id follows SP-1100 and stays outside producer semantics. The idempotency, event_id and CV-366
  key recipes are unchanged. Timestamps and retained originals, sweep 2026-11-11 (CV-1101 beside CV-253 and CV-317;
  SP-1101): every timestamp field uses the shared CV-1101 date_time predicate with its owner''s profile, never a
  lane grammar. occurred_at_utc and payload ts take the broad event_record profile (T or t, Z, z or an hh:mm
  offset, legitimate leap seconds, any fraction length); Storage-assigned observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc also
  take CV-253''s storage_utc_z profile (terminal uppercase Z only), on the current record, the retry original and
  retained history alike. A retry original and a retained history read are first resolved once through the shared
  SP-1101 RetainedDispatcher from Storage''s sealed write custody (static stand-in
  Plans/card2_original_custody.json, never a request field): a Store outside that custody refuses as
  original_unavailable and a sealed recipe without an installed frozen verifier as recipe_unknown, with no
  fallback, current-then-legacy probing or caller override. The only write-time recipe is card2@1, whose tuple pins
  the EventRecord and family payload schema bytes and these field profiles. Owner-valid lowercase, offset,
  leap-second and long-fraction history stays readable with its exact spelling; an offset or lowercase-z Storage

### CV-560 - FileManager exact payload routes

- file.copied@1.0.0: Plans/event_payloads/file_manager/file_copied.schema.json; semantic owner F-150.
- file.created@1.0.0: Plans/event_payloads/file_manager/file_created.schema.json; semantic owner F-151.
- file.deleted@1.0.0: Plans/event_payloads/file_manager/file_deleted.schema.json; semantic owner F-152.
- file.exported@1.0.0: Plans/event_payloads/file_manager/file_exported.schema.json; semantic owner F-153.
- file.moved@1.0.0: Plans/event_payloads/file_manager/file_moved.schema.json; semantic owner F-154.
- file.renamed@1.0.0: Plans/event_payloads/file_manager/file_renamed.schema.json; semantic owner F-155.
- folder.copied@1.0.0: Plans/event_payloads/file_manager/folder_copied.schema.json; semantic owner F-156.
- folder.created@1.0.0: Plans/event_payloads/file_manager/folder_created.schema.json; semantic owner F-157.
- folder.deleted@1.0.0: Plans/event_payloads/file_manager/folder_deleted.schema.json; semantic owner F-158.
- folder.exported@1.0.0: Plans/event_payloads/file_manager/folder_exported.schema.json; semantic owner F-159.
- folder.moved@1.0.0: Plans/event_payloads/file_manager/folder_moved.schema.json; semantic owner F-160.
- folder.renamed@1.0.0: Plans/event_payloads/file_manager/folder_renamed.schema.json; semantic owner F-161.
Each closed root is adopted independently under its own schema_id and schema_version. Opaque references resolve original owner receipt entries, never raw filesystem paths. No family is admitted.

The newly authored closed Plans/filemanager_operation_contracts.schema.json types operation_custody,
accepted_command, settlement, path_snapshot_entry and family_control are adopted by each own F unit
through SP-560. Accepted descriptor/store/epoch and settled payload/path originals are immutable;
only accepted -> effect_settled -> history_settled or accepted -> no_event_settled revision CAS
transitions are permitted; the latter has a closed noncompletion receipt and no completed event. Exact
receipt_ref/key, family/payload discriminator, command/envelope/scope, path coverage and source/
result/container joins are semantic requirements in addition to closed shape validation. Copy result
identity differs from source; create result differs from destination container, including native aliases.
Unknown schemas, unequal retries, unavailable originals, bad joins or late changes fence. The separate
SP-286/CV-339 full_value_request/full_value_result and strict v2 witness remain their original shapes;
resolve.v2 is semantic replay only and cannot establish full-value equality. SP-560 supplies literal
physical keys, resolvers, transaction fences, activation and coherent backup/restore; the generic
receipt_record_baseline supplies none of this authority. No admission is granted.

SP-560 also owns the closed physical operation_custody_value/family_control_value union and its
SP-337 whole-value reference branches; operation_custody/family_control remain resolved logical
contracts. Both physical profiles use canonical redb, coordination_and_storage and max_value_bytes=16384.
The BLAKE3/size/media reference spelling and canonical MessagePack boundary are explicit in SP-560.
A large event uses payload={} and payload_ref, resolving the complete closed family payload before
settlement joins while strict full-value proof keeps the original stored representation. Missing or
changed original pack bytes refuse reading, CAS and terminal publication. Terminal history_settled
binds the exact immutable settlement, original complete EventRecord, original receipt and strict
resolve_full_value.v1 request/result/v2 witness, not merely individually valid shapes. Current writer
and retry reject projector_replay_only with replay_only_not_appendable. CV-339 semantic retry equality
excludes Storage-assigned sequence_id/observed_at_utc/persisted_at_utc; original-value recovery does not.

Numbers follow CV-1100, SP-1100 and SP-1101 beside the existing CV-317, CV-339, SP-236, SP-286, SP-337 and
SP-339 owners. Each family's identity T stays the RFC 8785 string array of its F unit, qualified by CV-1100:
non-ASCII strings encode exactly and a lone surrogate refuses. The custody_v2 producer_semantic_digest is the
CV-317 producer projection under CV-1100 qualified JCS, so an integer whose binary64 value or emitted JCS
decimal differs from it (for example 2^53+1 or 2^60) refuses before any effect. Every declared integer slot of
a current write is an exact integer within its schema range, and bool, float or decimal values refuse there:
the payload path_snapshot_revision and descendant_count, operation recovery_epoch, revision and every
path_snapshot_revision, and control control_revision, last_admitted_sequence and writer_cutoff_sequence.
EventRecord bodies are measured and referenced with SP-1100 EVENT_VALUE (SP-236) bytes; operation and control
redb values keep SP-339 canonical MessagePack. A retained original is read with the recipe recorded when it
was written (SP-1101); current integer admission never narrows it.

Timestamps follow CV-1101 beside CV-253. Every format: date-time of these routes is checked by the shared
CV-1101 predicate, and a missing zone, a space separator, a trailing LF, an impossible date or clock field
and a false leap second refuse everywhere. The family payload ts, the companion accepted_at_utc and
settled_at_utc, the EventRecord occurred_at_utc and the AppendReceipt acknowledged_at_utc use its
event_record profile: lowercase t or z, offsets, real leap seconds and fractions of any length are accepted
and never rewritten. The Storage-assigned observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc of every EventRecord these
routes read also take CV-253's storage_utc_z profile, so an offset, a signed zero offset or a lowercase z
refuses there. occurred_at_utc and
settled_at_utc still equal payload ts as exact strings. A retained original is resolved through SP-1101: its
write-time edition and frozen resource manifest come only from Storage's sealed issuance custody, never from
the request; an original without that record is unavailable, and an edition or resource set with no installed
verifier is unsupported, each refused without trying the current recipe. The twelve families have one
write-time edition. Its frozen verifier applies the same CV-1101 and CV-253 profiles, so a format check that
was skipped in the past never admits an invalid original.

EventRecord remains pm.event.v0@2.0.0 with event_type=runtime_artifact.validation_test; payload.schema_id=pm.runtime_artifact.validation_test.schema.v1, payload.artifact_type=validation_test, payload.project_id equals the non-null project envelope identity. The closed schema's required and optional fields remain unchanged; optional metadata is not an identity fallback. App definitions under $defs (where present) remain separate explicitly selected source contracts under CV-366, not implicit Project-event alternatives.
  Envelope joins for this exact family: payload_schema_id equals the logical payload schema ID; replay_policy=dedupe_by_idempotency_key and redaction_profile=no_secrets. Explicitly adopt SP-337 store-once packs for this family. Newly authored exact dispatch binding under DL-045: encode the unchanged logical payload as RFC 8785 canonical JSON, UTF-8 without BOM/newline. At <=16,384 bytes store that object in payload and payload_ref=null. Above 16,384 bytes store payload={} and payload_ref as the exact string "pm.payload_pack.v1:blake3:<64 lowercase hex>:<canonical decimal byte size>:application/json"; byte size is the uncompressed canonical UTF-8 payload length. No base64 or inline body bypass is allowed. This string fits the existing EventRecord payload_ref type; it adds no envelope field or stored-value family. Decode the referenced exact bytes without duplicate keys, validate UTF-8/JSON and canonical encoding, verify BLAKE3 id, size and media type, then validate the resolved object against this family's unchanged closed logical schema before applying any joins or exposing metadata. The schema applies to the resolved object, never the external placeholder; all payload field joins below refer to that object. Reject nonempty placeholder, both/neither routes, noncanonical/wrong-size/wrong-digest/wrong-media/missing bytes or a wrong-family decoded schema. Pack bytes and index are durable before acknowledgement through SP-337's pack-first sync or same-group segment staging/seal protocol. Retained EventRecord references keep the full logical metadata reachable under DL-075 even when externalized; linked source bodies retain their own separate deletion/revocation policy. Current source authorization, holds and coherent backup/restore cover the pack reference and bytes; no recreation from a deleted linked body. Retries freeze the original payload route/ref/bytes as producer-semantic inputs; no repacking or re-encoding may silently change the original digest or first receipt. Envelope run_id/attempt_id/thread_id/node_id equal the corresponding payload values or required-present null for absent optional fields; occurred_at_utc equals payload.created_at_utc. actor_ref names the actual producer actor, not the viewer; observed_at_utc, persisted_at_utc and sequence_id remain Storage-owned. producer_semantic_digest uses the unchanged EventRecord producer-owned semantic-field recipe including its optional/null presence rules, never a hash of the complete envelope.
  RAP-118 owns the exact producer owner.runtime_artifacts.validation_test.publish@1.0.0, identity framing, original-source joins, privacy/deletion checks, compatibility and withdrawal. SP-538 explicitly adopts SP-278 and SP-286/CV-339 full-value v2 without inventing a physical value or giving the deferred artifact projector authority. Until a later separate exact registry admission, producer append is refused; these drafts register no family. Positive/negative schema and semantic oracles are Plans/runtime_artifact_event_drafts.fixtures.json and scripts/pm-runtime-artifact-event-drafts.py, owned by ATS-260. Native obligations remain NOT_RUN.

### CV-590 - Bundle Revision Requested Closed Event Contract

```yaml
plan_unit_id: CV-590
unit_type: requirement
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Contracts_V0.md
canonical_text: '`bundle.revision_requested` has payload schema Plans/event_payloads/bundle_revision/revision_requested.schema.json,
  schema_id pm.event_payload.bundle.revision_requested.v1, schema_version 1.0.0. All listed properties are required-present;
  safe_point_id is nullable and predecessor_event_id follows ACD-571. additionalProperties is false. annotation_ids
  is an ordered, unique, nonempty list of eligible durable annotations; preserve request order through every phase.
  requested_revision_capability is the actual non-secret capability identifier, never rewritten to the effective
  enum. ts is the original UTC instant of this phase, reused verbatim on retry. source_ref is an authorized immutable
  evidence reference; it never contains body text, a URL credential or a local absolute path. project_id/thread_id/bundle_id/revision_id
  and permission_snapshot_id must resolve through their existing owners. Project scope is mandatory: EventRecord
  scope_kind=project, project_id and thread_id equal payload values, run_id/attempt_id are null; application or
  focus fallback is refused. actor_ref names the authenticated review owner for request, targeted revision runner
  otherwise. correlation_id=revision_id and causation_event_id=predecessor_event_id. payload follows the SP-337 representation below, redaction_profile=secret_refs_only,
  replay_policy=dedupe_by_idempotency_key.


  NEW technical identity contract under DL-045: identity bytes are UTF-8 of the compact JSON array ["bundle.revision_requested",project_id,thread_id,bundle_id,revision_id,phase_sequence]
  with ensure_ascii=false and separators comma/colon; digest=SHA-256 of those bytes. event_id="evt_bundle_revision_"+digest
  and idempotency_key="bundle.revision_requested:"+digest. Original timestamp, ordered annotations, capability fields,
  permission snapshot and source evidence are frozen at preparation. Retry uses the same full EventRecord and producer
  semantic digest; same identity with any changed semantic value is a conflict. A distinct new request gets a fresh
  revision_id with existing source-owned lineage. Interrupted revision recovery preserves revision_id and uses the
  next phase_sequence; completed revisions never reopen by replay. NEW technical phase_sequence is a nonnegative
  integer: request is zero; every later phase is exactly predecessor.phase_sequence+1. Under the existing revision
  recovery writer fence, predecessor must be the latest committed event for this exact revision, not an arbitrary
  older start. An interrupted revision may start again with the same revision_id, a new phase_sequence and the interrupted
  event as predecessor; completed never starts again. Every retry preserves the prepared sequence; unresolved source/receipt
  custody cannot allocate a replacement sequence. Same-lifecycle predecessor, annotation order, capabilities and
  snapshot joins must hold before append. ACD-571 defines this family''s phase predicate; SP-575 defines the exact
  receipt/read/withdrawal protocol. Unsupported payload versions fail closed, never coerce or alias sibling payloads.
  The schema is prepared without registry admission. Normal append refuses projector_replay_only as replay_only_not_appendable;
  compatibility history remains passive and cannot select the writer. EventRecord follows Contracts_V0.md#EventRecord
  and Plans/event_record.schema.json, without a local envelope schema. Envelope event_type and payload_schema_id
  equal this exact payload; node_id, requested_account_ref and effective_account_ref are null; all
  migration fields are null for current native writes; parent_event_id equals predecessor_event_id, producer_sequence_id
  equals phase_sequence, occurred_at_utc equals ts. Actor is the original authenticated owner frozen in SP-579 source,
  not a reader or retry actor. Storage alone assigns sequence/observed/persisted fields. Source/result/prepared-event
  equality is mandatory under SP-579.


  NEW SP-337 event-body binding for bundle.revision_requested under DL-045: measure the complete logical body using the exact SP-026 canonical MessagePack bytes Storage stores, never JSON character or serialized JSON size. At most 16,384 bytes (including exactly 16,384) uses that closed logical body inline and payload_ref=null. A larger body cannot append inline: payload is the empty object selected by this schema''s #/$defs/referenced_stub and payload_ref is the UTF-8 compact sorted-key JSON descriptor string {"blake3":"<64 lowercase hex>","byte_size":<encoded byte count>,"media_type":"application/vnd.puppetmaster.event.bundle-revision-requested+msgpack"}. #/$defs/payload_reference closes the descriptor; byte_size is at least 16,385, and the BLAKE3 length is exactly 64, so a trailing LF is invalid. This string representation preserves the shared EventRecord shape. CV-1100 governs raw current tokens and each declared integer slot: -0, decimal/exponent tokens, string numbers, booleans and other wrong types refuse without coercion; 01 and -01 are invalid JSON. The family identity retains its exact compact UTF-8 JSON array, ensure_ascii=false and comma/colon separators; the descriptor retains sorted-key compact integer JSON. These local recipes keep their existing IDs, fields and tuple order. CV-317/CV-1100 governs the complete producer-semantic JCS projection and qualifies its exact binary64 and emitted decimal values before effects; it does not impose a source-schema cap. SP-026/SP-236/SP-1100 governs full physical EventRecord/source bytes and CV-339 commitments, preserving the full owner uint64 domain, finite float kind and signed zero where the selected original schema allows them. SP-278 keeps its separate binding wrapper/profile. SP-286/SP-1101 selects one authenticated original schema/resource/number recipe outside request data for retained reads and original receipt recovery; current token/type admission never narrows a lawful retained original. Current caller retry admission remains separate from verifying that original. Descriptor text must equal that canonical encoding, so alternate spelling, key order, whitespace, duplicate keys or escaped numeric text refuses. phase_sequence and byte_size use this same integer-only domain in local and composed validators. Every original-value, prepared-event, source and receipt join compares exact nested types and canonical bytes, never language numeric equality. Every boolean guard checks the exact boolean type before its value; payloads retain their closed object type. It contains metadata only, never a base64 body. payload_schema_id continues to identify this family''s complete logical body, which the reader validates against the same closed payload schema after reference resolution. Verify readable original pack bytes, exact size, BLAKE3, this exact media type, canonical encoding and all original source/identity/actor/causality joins; pack bytes and their index must be durable before the referencing append or successful publication. Missing, corrupt, substituted, wrong-size/type, unreadable or undurable content refuses without append or checkpoint advancement. Source-record overflow references are independent and cannot stand in for this event reference. Freeze this representation and descriptor at original preparation; producer-semantic comparison includes the stored payload and payload_ref, excludes Storage-assigned metadata, and preserves the original full value, commitment and first receipt on retry. Read, compatibility, rebuild and restore resolve the same bytes without rerunning the owner. A compatibility view may change replay_policy only; authenticate every other supplied field against the retained original before checking its recorded full-value commitment and receipt. Historical reads recheck current access/deletion and reader withdrawal, not current writer CAS/effect eligibility. Coherent backup and admitted restore include every reachable event pack/index, exact digest/size/media-type inventory and original source/event/receipt dependencies; missing event-payload inventory fences. No truncation, product limit, retention/deletion answer or admission is added.'

canonical_text: '`bundle.revision_interrupted` has payload schema Plans/event_payloads/bundle_revision/revision_interrupted.schema.json,
  schema_id pm.event_payload.bundle.revision_interrupted.v1, schema_version 1.0.0. All listed properties are required-present;
  safe_point_id is nullable and predecessor_event_id follows ACD-574. additionalProperties is false. annotation_ids
  is an ordered, unique, nonempty list of eligible durable annotations; preserve request order through every phase.
  requested_revision_capability is the actual non-secret capability identifier, never rewritten to the effective
  enum. ts is the original UTC instant of this phase, reused verbatim on retry. source_ref is an authorized immutable
  evidence reference; it never contains body text, a URL credential or a local absolute path. project_id/thread_id/bundle_id/revision_id
  and permission_snapshot_id must resolve through their existing owners. Project scope is mandatory: EventRecord
  scope_kind=project, project_id and thread_id equal payload values, run_id/attempt_id are null; application or
  focus fallback is refused. actor_ref names the authenticated review owner for request, targeted revision runner
  otherwise. correlation_id=revision_id and causation_event_id=predecessor_event_id. payload follows the SP-337 representation below, redaction_profile=secret_refs_only,
  replay_policy=dedupe_by_idempotency_key.


  NEW technical identity contract under DL-045: identity bytes are UTF-8 of the compact JSON array ["bundle.revision_interrupted",project_id,thread_id,bundle_id,revision_id,phase_sequence]
  with ensure_ascii=false and separators comma/colon; digest=SHA-256 of those bytes. event_id="evt_bundle_revision_"+digest
  and idempotency_key="bundle.revision_interrupted:"+digest. Original timestamp, ordered annotations, capability
  fields, permission snapshot and source evidence are frozen at preparation. Retry uses the same full EventRecord
  and producer semantic digest; same identity with any changed semantic value is a conflict. A distinct new request
  gets a fresh revision_id with existing source-owned lineage. Interrupted revision recovery preserves revision_id
  and uses the next phase_sequence; completed revisions never reopen by replay. NEW technical phase_sequence is
  a nonnegative integer: request is zero; every later phase is exactly predecessor.phase_sequence+1. Under the existing
  revision recovery writer fence, predecessor must be the latest committed event for this exact revision, not an
  arbitrary older start. An interrupted revision may start again with the same revision_id, a new phase_sequence
  and the interrupted event as predecessor; completed never starts again. Every retry preserves the prepared sequence;
  unresolved source/receipt custody cannot allocate a replacement sequence. Same-lifecycle predecessor, annotation
  order, capabilities and snapshot joins must hold before append. ACD-574 defines this family''s phase predicate;
  SP-578 defines the exact receipt/read/withdrawal protocol. Unsupported payload versions fail closed, never coerce
  or alias sibling payloads. The schema is prepared without registry admission. Normal append refuses projector_replay_only
  as replay_only_not_appendable; compatibility history remains passive and cannot select the writer. EventRecord
  follows Contracts_V0.md#EventRecord and Plans/event_record.schema.json, without a local envelope schema. Envelope
  event_type and payload_schema_id equal this exact payload; node_id, requested_account_ref and effective_account_ref
  are null; all migration fields are null for current native writes; parent_event_id equals predecessor_event_id,
  producer_sequence_id equals phase_sequence, occurred_at_utc equals ts. Actor is the original authenticated owner
  frozen in SP-579 source, not a reader or retry actor. Storage alone assigns sequence/observed/persisted fields.
  Source/result/prepared-event equality is mandatory under SP-579.


  NEW SP-337 event-body binding for bundle.revision_interrupted under DL-045: measure the complete logical body using the exact SP-026 canonical MessagePack bytes Storage stores, never JSON character or serialized JSON size. At most 16,384 bytes (including exactly 16,384) uses that closed logical body inline and payload_ref=null. A larger body cannot append inline: payload is the empty object selected by this schema''s #/$defs/referenced_stub and payload_ref is the UTF-8 compact sorted-key JSON descriptor string {"blake3":"<64 lowercase hex>","byte_size":<encoded byte count>,"media_type":"application/vnd.puppetmaster.event.bundle-revision-interrupted+msgpack"}. #/$defs/payload_reference closes the descriptor; byte_size is at least 16,385, and the BLAKE3 length is exactly 64, so a trailing LF is invalid. This string representation preserves the shared EventRecord shape. CV-1100 governs raw current tokens and each declared integer slot: -0, decimal/exponent tokens, string numbers, booleans and other wrong types refuse without coercion; 01 and -01 are invalid JSON. The family identity retains its exact compact UTF-8 JSON array, ensure_ascii=false and comma/colon separators; the descriptor retains sorted-key compact integer JSON. These local recipes keep their existing IDs, fields and tuple order. CV-317/CV-1100 governs the complete producer-semantic JCS projection and qualifies its exact binary64 and emitted decimal values before effects; it does not impose a source-schema cap. SP-026/SP-236/SP-1100 governs full physical EventRecord/source bytes and CV-339 commitments, preserving the full owner uint64 domain, finite float kind and signed zero where the selected original schema allows them. SP-278 keeps its separate binding wrapper/profile. SP-286/SP-1101 selects one authenticated original schema/resource/number recipe outside request data for retained reads and original receipt recovery; current token/type admission never narrows a lawful retained original. Current caller retry admission remains separate from verifying that original. Descriptor text must equal that canonical encoding, so alternate spelling, key order, whitespace, duplicate keys or escaped numeric text refuses. phase_sequence and byte_size use this same integer-only domain in local and composed validators. Every original-value, prepared-event, source and receipt join compares exact nested types and canonical bytes, never language numeric equality. Every boolean guard checks the exact boolean type before its value; payloads retain their closed object type. It contains metadata only, never a base64 body. payload_schema_id continues to identify this family''s complete logical body, which the reader validates against the same closed payload schema after reference resolution. Verify readable original pack bytes, exact size, BLAKE3, this exact media type, canonical encoding and all original source/identity/actor/causality joins; pack bytes and their index must be durable before the referencing append or successful publication. Missing, corrupt, substituted, wrong-size/type, unreadable or undurable content refuses without append or checkpoint advancement. Source-record overflow references are independent and cannot stand in for this event reference. Freeze this representation and descriptor at original preparation; producer-semantic comparison includes the stored payload and payload_ref, excludes Storage-assigned metadata, and preserves the original full value, commitment and first receipt on retry. Read, compatibility, rebuild and restore resolve the same bytes without rerunning the owner. A compatibility view may change replay_policy only; authenticate every other supplied field against the retained original before checking its recorded full-value commitment and receipt. Historical reads recheck current access/deletion and reader withdrawal, not current writer CAS/effect eligibility. Coherent backup and admitted restore include every reachable event pack/index, exact digest/size/media-type inventory and original source/event/receipt dependencies; missing event-payload inventory fences. No truncation, product limit, retention/deletion answer or admission is added.'

### CV-596 - Planning Run wizard.blocked Complete Event Contract

```yaml
plan_unit_id: CV-596
unit_type: requirement
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Contracts_V0.md
canonical_text: 'NEWLY AUTHORED OWNER CONTRACT for wizard.blocked under DL-045 and DL-431; prepared without admission.
  Exact family membership remains ABSENT in Plans/event_family_registry.json: neither this unit nor its schema permits
  a current writer until individual registry admission. Semantic owner is current Plans/Planning_Wizard.md#PWIZ-002,
  extended for this exact event by this unit; payload/persistence binding is this unit plus CV-233. Jared''s only
  quoted words are "i approve all of it". The deck''s approve-all mapping selects A, as recorded in landed Plans/Decision_Log.md#DL-431.
  Answer source is /mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/ANSWERS_E-CARDS-2_20261105.md;
  frozen deck E-CARDS-2.as-presented-6db25be3.md SHA-256 6db25be3dd290ab0083af482383e469a78dc109a037ad0fd0ece5d8f15679b30.
  The approved option''s explanatory prose is the card''s text, not a Jared quotation.


  Under DL-431 (deck-2 Card 4.a option A), attach Blocked to the whole Planning Run. Save it only when the component
  responsible for planning records a blockage or repair attempt that prevents every otherwise permitted next step.
  A stalled topic does not block the run if another can continue. Count completed repair attempts for that blockage;
  add no three-round trigger. You see the whole run''s blockage and report. This applies to the current Planning
  Wizard, successor of the retired Chain Wizard, not a restored wizard-status lifecycle. wizard_id is the PlanningRun
  planning_run_id; thread_id is nullable incidental context and never selects a topic as the blocked subject. Existing
  route_target owns navigation and blocked/remediation owns the episode identity: blockage_id is that exact owner
  episode, never a new runtime/node identity. CV-233''s report_ref and optional detail refs remain inspection only;
  resume_url is serialized route_target transport, not another navigation primitive.


  All properties of Plans/event_payloads/planning_wizard/wizard_blocked.schema.json are required-present, root additionalProperties=false,
  schema_id=pm.event_payload.wizard.blocked.v1 and schema_version=1.0.0. Preserve CV-233 minima wizard_id, nullable
  thread_id, round_count, report_ref, resume_url and ts. Added project_id, planning_run_id, blockage_id, observation_id,
  source_ref, permission_snapshot_id, predecessor_event_id and route_target_ref bind the actual original observation;
  route_target_ref must resolve through the existing route owner to the same Project/PlanningRun and exact resume_url.
  Reports/routes require independent current access and availability. No report body, prompt, secret, credential,
  raw local path or topic-status snapshot is copied into the event.


  Producer emitter.wizard_blocked@1.0.0 is the responsible Planning Wizard component''s observer of its original
  planning result. It explicitly adopts SP-286 and CV-339 full-value v2 first-AppendReceipt custody, SP-336/SP-347
  durability and Case L-2/SP-026/SP-236 original frame bytes. Before append require exact family/version admission,
  original observation/permission/current PlanningRun reservation, then commit the original observation and freeze
  the complete EventRecord. Append via Storage; resolve the independently issued original full event, semantic digest,
  full-value commitment, first receipt and durable group before publishing recorded success or allowing a dependent
  observation. A lost acknowledgement resolves the original, never re-executes planning, repair or the clearing
  action. Missing original/dedupe proof is unavailable; changed semantics is idempotency_conflict; unknown effect
  fences publication and goes to the existing owner''s recovery. A confirmed older restore does not replay lost
  post-backup work.


  Scope is project-only, using a real Project under PWIZ-002; application/no-project writes refuse. Adopt Plans/event_record.schema.json
  unchanged. Envelope project_id/thread_id equal payload; runtime run_id/node_id/attempt_id, account refs and producer_sequence_id
  are null. actor_ref is the authenticated original planning observation actor; occurred_at_utc=ts; correlation_id=blockage_id;
  causation_event_id=parent_event_id=predecessor_event_id; payload_schema_id identifies the decoded logical body;
  redaction_profile=secret_refs_only; current replay_policy=dedupe_by_idempotency_key; native migration fields are
  null. Storage alone assigns sequence/observed/persisted values and original receipt metadata. NEW identity recipe
  for wizard.blocked: lowercase SHA-256 of the existing UTF-8 compact JSON string-only array ["wizard.blocked",project_id,planning_run_id,blockage_id,observation_id],
  ensure_ascii=false and comma/colon separators. event_id="evt_wizard_blocked_"+digest; idempotency_key="wizard.blocked:"+digest.
  observation_id is the responsible component''s immutable observation identity reused on delivery/retry, never
  a reader-generated request. It is independent of incidental thread focus. source_ref="wizard_blocked_evidence:"+digest.
  All observed source/actor/causality/time/body/ref fields freeze at preparation.


  Retry compares exactly the producer-owned semantic fields enumerated by CV-339: event_type, scope_kind, project_id,
  thread_id, run_id, node_id, attempt_id, actor_ref, requested_account_ref, effective_account_ref, occurred_at_utc,

This is the own source schema's payload_reference root; it adds no envelope field, storage family or public API. Independently resolve exact canonical body bytes by that BLAKE3 address and verify digest, byte length, media type, complete semantic schema and original-source joins before acceptance. Selected bytes and their index entry must be durable before the referencing event is acknowledged; missing, changed, noncanonical or non-durable payload custody refuses. Synthetic payloads/durable_payload_ids model that boundary only; native packs, holds, access checks and durability remain NOT_RUN. Verify the same inline limit and reference custody on every retained issued/retained-boundary EventRecord used by recovery, terminal publication, retry or rebuild, even after original domain controls are disposed. Do not copy the resolved large body into any stored EventRecord, and do not replace an oversized body by an unchecked reference string. The source's original_request, original_result, writer_epoch, storage_instance_id, original_commit_ref and body_members must come from genuine producer custody before the EventRecord exists. Full request and result identities, exact accepted scope and execution context join; the request fields `guard_type`, `normalized_command_identity`, `segment_index`, `permission_snapshot_id`, `filesafe_scope_ref` join the result where applicable. Exact required body roles are `guard_input`, `guard_decision`; each is a non-secret ref plus original-byte SHA-256. The native source reader verifies the exact original storage record/codecs and evidence, including authentic Project FileSafe originals for snapshot/journal subjects; the new application view never rebinds those bytes or converts Project history.

Application `accepted_source_sha256` uses CV-366 accepted_source on the closed preimage {schema_id, schema_version, scope, semantic_record, immutable_identity}: semantic_record is this entire source with only accepted_source_sha256 omitted; immutable_identity is {source_ref, storage_instance_id, operation_id}. Project views commit the same closed preimage by SHA-256 of canonical MessagePack as an additional view commitment, preserving every original Project hash/codec underneath. Neither hash authenticates acceptance or replaces the original native source hash. Graph hashes use CV-366 source_graph excluding only graph_sha256.

**Lifecycle barriers for `filesafe.command_denied`.**

| From | To | Required barrier |
|---|---|---|
